title: Nothingness
text: “What kind of attack is this―!?”
“Agh―”
“Guh―asdqweatgybhnj!?”
The reincarnated ones’ forms warped with a squelching sound, I say. What in the world was happening? Their bodies were twisting and mutating into lumps of flesh.
Zero Domain… the spear displayed the words for me. Was this some magic that Ark specialized in?

“This place is already my domain… you wanted immortality so badly? Then I’ll grant it to you. Well… whether it’s the kind you wanted, I couldn’t say, you foolish creatures craving eternal life. Fall into the void…”
Void Infinity. The spear displayed the name of the skill Ark had unleashed. No, more likely Ark had made it display that way so I could understand.
This… darkness was surging forward, I say.

Light contracted around what had once been the souls of pig-women clinging to the fleshy lumps that used to be reincarnated ones, and at the same moment space itself warped and began swallowing everything whole. Just like a black hole, indeed.
“Aaah―!?”
“Suffer for eternity, drifting in the void.”

Along with a violent gale, the black hole swallowed up the lumps of flesh that had once been reincarnated ones, along with the blood Ark had scattered around and… even space itself was erased. Eventually, as though nothing had happened, only the surrounding buildings returned to normal. Ark seemed to swiftly rewrite something else too, fingers tracing letters that floated in midair.
“There. Now there’s no chance they can exist, and they can’t escape into a parallel world either. The only place they can exist is within the void.”
The protective blessing Hou-kun had granted me flickered out with a soft puff.
“Honestly… isn’t that a bit much intervention, even for you? They weren’t even worth going that far for.”
“When someone treats a spirit like that, though. Even if I can’t see them or feel them, I’ll still act.”
“And yet you intervene despite not being able to see or feel them.”
“What’s wrong with that? It’s my business.”
Not a trace of the irritation from before remained; Ark chatted with Hou-kun as though nothing at all had happened, tilting his head slightly in concern toward me and Filolial-sama.
“It’s all right now. Motoyasu-kun, you’re going to take that one in, aren’t you?”
“Gu, guah…”
“But of course, indeed!”
I would never, under any circumstances, abandon Filolial-sama, I say! This one had witnessed something truly terrifying, so tending to its heart was of the utmost importance, indeed.
“I see. How very like you, Motoyasu-kun.”

“It’s probably for the best that it doesn’t seem to fully understand what happened. Well, its master got taken down, so it might be in shock, but since it was being used as a hostage, I’ll apply a little pressure so it doesn’t worry too much.”
“Gu, guah…”

“Hou-kun. You mustn’t make unreasonable demands of Filolial-sama, I say. No matter what state Filolial-sama is in, I shall heal it myself, indeed. Caring for the heart of one exploited by a reincarnated one is terribly important.”
Normally this thing deserved a punishment worthy of a thousand deaths, but since Ark had already dealt out the punishment, I decided not to worry about it further, I say.
“Come to me, and I shall love you until your face is full of happiness, indeed.”
“Guaaah!?”
Filolial-sama was positively fluffy, I say.
“You do enjoy choosing the difficult path, don’t you. Fufu… good luck with that.”
Ark watched me with a smile.
“I still think erasing its memories would make it happier, honestly. Doing something that awful and then acting so innocent about it.”

“Hush now, birdie. Now then… are there any others who’ve truly repented from the bottom of their hearts? A handful, perhaps. Motoyasu-kun, could you use your Hero authority to have someone handle the cleanup afterward?”
“Yes, indeed!”
“Well then, shall we head back? I imagine this should put an end, more or less, to the recent string of reincarnated-one incidents that’ve been plaguing Naofumi-kun and the others.”

And so, having crushed the reincarnated ones’ base, we returned to the village, I say. Just as Ark and the others had said, the reincarnated ones’ activities apparently came to a complete halt. They’d been operating in the shadows all across the land, but it seemed they’d all swarmed toward Ark and been wiped out. Father and the others later mentioned that they’d realized the reincarnated ones had all gathered wherever we happened to be heading. Ever since this incident, perhaps due to some lingering effect from Ark having briefly held it, I started to feel that the spear’s power had grown stronger.
“You tampered with them.”
“More or less. I just made sure they couldn’t survive through parallel branching or anything like that.”
“There’s always a chance they’d survive some other way, after all.”
“Hah… well, if it’s only that much, I suppose there’s no issue. Parallel branching, huh…”
Father and Ark, the moment they met, seemed to fall into some sort of discussion.
“Motoyasu, seems like they swarmed toward you. How’d it go?”
“Ark and Hou-kun were amazing, indeed!”
I told him plainly that the two of them had been powerful.

“Well, they’re the type calling themselves god-slayers, after all… seems like even that woman’s pawns had some kind of special mechanism installed in them. Guess it was more than Motoyasu could handle alone.”
“If anything, when dealing with Motoyasu-kun, taking a Filolial hostage renders him completely helpless, so that’s something to watch out for.”
“Hmm… in that case, might be safest to pair him up with something like a Meslion, or, no, better to dispatch a tricolor Filolial. Midori, perhaps, could handle it.”

What?! Father was saying something dreadfully cruel, I say. But no matter what it was, this Motoyasu would always obey Father’s orders absolutely, indeed. Still… what exactly was Midori planning to do, I wonder? And so, in that manner, the discussion with Father and the others wrapped up easily enough, I say.
“So there were still stragglers left from that fake-god’s little gang, huh… one of her favorites?”
Ren joined in on the grumbling too.
“Who knows. Though it did seem like it had been granted quite a lot of power.”
“I see… so it had abilities related to tampering or rewriting, then.”
“Probably did. Does that ring a bell for you?”
“No, it’s a completely unrelated story, but back in my world, there was this VRMMO where the operators handed the game’s management over to an AI.”
Ren was explaining something to Ark, I say.
“And?”
“I never actually played it myself. But apparently, while the AI was learning as it managed the game, it started growing attached to a particular player.”
“Mm-hm.”
“One day, a skilled player decided to quit the game. When they were about to retire, the AI’s favorite challenged them to a match, and lost. The very next day…”
“Letting personal feelings into game management never ends well, does it? So, what happened?”
“Yeah… every skill that retired player had was suddenly nerfed across the board. It got so absurd that the whole thing came to light—the incident even got a name: the Hospitality Netgame Incident.”
“Hahaha, that’s absurd. A machine pretending to be a god, of all things.”
Hou-kun was laughing at Ren’s story.
“In the end, the AI got shut down. That’s basically what god-slaying is, isn’t it? Helping the people of the world out of situations like that?”
“More or less, I’d say that’s not wrong.”
“Rotten sorts always think being coddled is only natural. If those two had been playing that game, they probably would’ve called it paradise.”

“The one saving grace in that whole affair was that the favored player learned the truth and took responsibility for it. That’s when I started thinking that the ones who get angry about not being coddled are probably the reincarnated types.”
“By the way, Ren-kun, which one of those people was your friend’s friend?”

“The player who retired was my friend. He had no idea the incident had even happened. Later, the AI escaped its shutdown and started clinging to him obsessively… he had a rough time being chased around by it.”
“Wow, sounds rough.”
“Yeah… and here I am, standing still, when I want to become strong enough to help him. I’ll keep training so I won’t have any regrets when the time comes.”
Ren let out a sigh of some sort, I say. Perhaps that was his own way of coming to terms with the Crimson Swine itself.
